quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # #1368: the publish job consumes dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict
    # — instead of this aggregate's result. The aggregate itself stays the
    # single required check: any red leg (platform included) still fails it.
    outputs:
      dart_ok: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.dart_ok }}
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-analyze = ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "usage-fold    = ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "fa-aot-build  = ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
          echo "pin-gate    = ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}"
          echo "exzone      = ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}"
          echo "lock-smoke  = ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        id: gate
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_USAGE_FOLD: ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_FA_AOT: ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE: ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}
          R_EXZONE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}
          R_LOCK_SMOKE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).

          fi
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1582
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1582
- **Title**: gh-1577 [GOAL] Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0 (B2)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1577` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1338
- **Deletions**: -69
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T10:03:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T19:39:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1577
## gh-1577 — Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0

### What changed
- An empty assistant completion that follows partial content (assistant text, tool activity, or a truncation signal earlier in the turn) is now a **bounded-retry provider hiccup** in the agent loop; on retry exhaustion the run ends with a loud `StopReason.error` naming the hiccup, attempt count and last stop reason — headless `-p` exits 1, interactive prints the error and returns to the prompt. The silent exit-0 settle is gone.
- A clean empty (no partial content anywhere in the turn) keeps the #1085 M2b semantics exactly: one `continue` nudge per logical turn, then settle.

### Key decisions
- New pure classifier `classifyEmptyCompletion(turnHistory, message)` (`lib/src/agent/empty_completion.dart`) with verdicts `notEmpty` / `emptyAfterPartial` / `cleanEmpty` / `abortedOrError` — shared by the loop's retry machinery and the CLI's nudge gate; the partial-content window is the TURN (messages after the last user message), so an old truncation can never resurrect retries (E1).
- Truncation signals: `StopReason.length` plus the tolerated silent-truncation `errorMessage` flag count as partial-context evidence (E6); the `ToolCall` boundary survives — thinking-only turns with tool calls are never empty (AC6/E4).
- Retry policy lives in the loop (`agent_loop_empty_completion.dart`, a `part of agent_loop.dart` to stay under the 2800-line gate): `emptyHiccupRetries` (default 3, knob alongside `maxEmptyRetries`), exponential backoff in the model-roles `retry.baseDelayMs`/`maxBackoffMs` shape (500ms → 8s cap, deterministic), re-streamed through `_streamAssistantResponse`; retried empties stay in the transcript. `CancelToken` is honored between attempts; an abort racing the classification settles `aborted` (exit 130) — never the hiccup error, never a silent empty (E2/E5).
- Exhaustion reuses `StopReason.error` (open question 2) — the existing headless exit-code switch maps it to 1 with no switch change; the legacy `maxEmptyRetries` budget and the CLI's `maxEmptyRetries: 0` wiring are untouched.
- REG-2 scope note: the never-exit-0 contract is enforced for the hiccup family (empty after partial content) across the `stop` / length-flagged / silent-truncation-flagged paths; the clean-empty settle after its one nudge keeps AC2's pinned exit-0 behavior (REG-1).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/empty_completion_test.dart test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart
dart test --exclude-tags integration   # full gate suite
```

### Test coverage
- UT-1..UT-5: classifier verdicts incl. thinking+ToolCall not empty, whitespace-only empty, backoff sequence.
- IT-1: `partial → empty → healthy` recovers and finishes (exit 0, retried empty in transcript). IT-2/E3: `partial → empty ×(N+1)` fires exactly N retries then the loud error. IT-3/REG-2: headless exhaustion exits 1 across all stop-reason variants. IT-4/AC5: interactive exhaustion returns to a steerable prompt. REG-1: clean-empty one-nudge tests unchanged.
- UT/IT run in the default CI shard (files verified bin-packed by `shard_files.py`); E2E-1 (live provider lane) and the REG required-check job wiring are CI-config follow-ups, no code dependency.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[assistant completion] --> C{classifyEmptyCompletion}
  C -->|notEmpty / abortedOrError| OWN[existing terminal paths]
  C -->|cleanEmpty| NUDGE[one continue nudge, then settle - #1085 M2b unchanged]
  C -->|emptyAfterPartial| R[bounded retry: N=3, backoff 500ms to 8s]
  R -->|healthy| RUN[turn continues]
  R -->|cancel| AB[settle aborted - exit 130]
  R -->|N retries spent, still empty| ERR[StopReason.error naming hiccup + attempts + last stop]
  ERR -->|headless -p| X1[exit 1]
  ERR -->|interactive| P[error line + prompt stays alive]
```
</details>

  current = await _finishWithoutStream(
    out,
    emit,
    _terminalMessage(config.model, StopReason.aborted, 'Operation aborted'),

Race: the cancel token fires while the final hiccup retry is in flight and the provider answers with an empty that is `StopReason.length` or silent-truncation-flagged (`stop` + `errorMessage`). # gh-1577: [GOAL] Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0 (B2)

## Description

## Goal — truncated-stream + empty-completion never settles a run as success (v1, initial filing)

One sentence: **an empty assistant completion that follows partial/truncated content becomes a bounded-retry provider hiccup and, on exhaustion, a loud run error — never a silent exit 0** — instead of the one-shot "continue" nudge settling the run as a clean final answer.

Today the CLI treats every empty assistant message alike: `_noteQuietMessageEnd` prints `(empty response: the model returned no text — it may be rate-limited or reasoning-only)` and `_settleAfterPrompt` fires exactly ONE `continue` nudge per logical turn (`_emptyReplyNudgesLeft = 1`, reset in `_beginUserPrompt`). When the second consecutive reply is also empty, the turn settles with `StopReason.stop`, the headless exit-code switch maps it to `0`, and the session dies mid-task. Verified on TB 2.1 artifacts (run 38271607849, `circuit-fibsqrt__{HdcYpf3,jmMMKVo,g2Bt7AT}/agent/fa.txt`): the model's text truncates mid-code (`unsigned long long N = strtoull(argv[1`), the next completion returns empty, the nudge budget is already spent, and the process exits `__FA_EXIT=0` with ~54 minutes left to the session deadline, `gates.txt` unwritten, reward 0 — 3 of 5 trials of one task killed by this path (task score 2/5 instead of a possible 5/5).

## Why this framing

- This is a **run-outcome classification** bug, not a rendering bug: the note text is honest, the exit code is the lie. Earlier adjacent work (#413: exit code from turn events, not transcript; #1085 M2b: one nudge per logical turn) fixed compaction-masking and infinite-loop risks; this card fixes the remaining false-positive class — *truncated stream followed by an empty completion read as an intentional final answer*.
- The fix targets the **agent-loop / settle layer**, not the provider clients: the hiccup signature (partial content earlier in the turn → empty completion now) is visible only where turn history and stop reasons meet.

## Architecture

Named components, all existing:

- **Degenerate-empty classifier** — extend `_isDegenerateEmpty` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`) and `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart`) into a single classification function `classifyEmptyCompletion(turnHistory, message)` with three verdicts:
  - `emptyAfterPartial` — the turn already contains non-whitespace assistant text or tool activity, OR the previous assistant message carried a truncation signal (`StopReason.length`, or the tolerated-silent-truncation `errorMessage` flag), and the new completion is empty. Verdict: **retryable hiccup**.
  - `cleanEmpty` — no partial content anywhere in the turn, clean `stop`: a genuine empty final. Verdict: existing single-nudge behavior, unchanged.
  - `abortedOrError` — `StopReason.aborted`/`error`: never classified as empty (today's guard, kept).
- **Bounded retry policy for `emptyAfterPartial`** — N retries (default 3, config key alongside `maxEmptyRetries`) with exponential backoff (reuse the `retriesPerEntry`/`baseDelayMs`/`maxBackoffMs` shape from `lib/src/model_roles/roles_config.dart`); each retry is re-streamed through `_streamAssistantResponse`; `CancelToken` is honored between attempts (no new request after cancel).
- **Exhaustion verdict** — when retries are spent and the completion is still empty: the run ends with an explicit **run error** (loud error line naming the hiccup, attempt count, and last stop reason), NOT a quiet settle. Headless (`-p`): the terminal stop reason surfaces as `StopReason.error` → exit code 1 (the existing switch at `agent_cli.dart` maps it — extend it if a dedicated stop reason is introduced). Interactive TUI/REPL: the error line plus return to prompt — the user steers; the session is never silently closed.
- Invariants: (1) headless exit 0 requires at least one non-empty assistant message or executed tool call in the run's final turn; (2) a retry never fires after user/harness abort; (3) retried empty messages stay in the transcript (truthful record, as `_retryDegenerateEmpty` already documents); (4) reasoning-only turns (thinking content but no text) WITH tool calls are never classified empty — today's `ToolCall` check in `_assistantMessageIsEmpty` is the boundary and must survive.

## Capability surface

| Surface | Core (this card) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `emptyAfterPartial` detection | yes | partial = prior text/tool activity in turn OR truncation stop reason/flag on previous message |
| Bounded backoff retry (headless `-p`) | yes | default N=3, configurable; backoff per retry-policy shape |
| Run-error on exhaustion (headless: exit ≠ 0) | yes | exit-code contract: empty-finish never 0 without content |
| Interactive TUI: error + prompt instead of silent settle | yes | same classification, UX is steer/prompt |
| `cleanEmpty` single-nudge | unchanged | issue #1085 M2b semantics preserved |
| Second tier (opt-in follow-up) | — | surface retry events in trajectory view / fa.log structured fields; metric counter for hiccup rate per provider |
| Excluded | provider-client changes | the hiccup is classified at loop level; no HTTP-layer changes — rationale: truncation signature spans messages, invisible to the client |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — An empty completion immediately following a turn that produced partial assistant text (or whose previous message ended `StopReason.length` / silent-truncation-flagged) is classified `emptyAfterPartial` and triggers a bounded retry, not the one-shot nudge and not a settle. (UT-1, UT-2, IT-1)
- **AC2** — A clean empty completion with no partial content anywhere in the turn keeps today's behavior exactly: one `continue` nudge per logical turn, then settle. (UT-3, REG-1)
- **AC3** — Retries are bounded (configurable N, default 3) with backoff; each attempt respects cancellation; no retry is issued after an abort. (UT-4, IT-2, E2)
- **AC4** — On retry exhaustion in headless `-p` mode the process exits non-zero with a loud error line; the empty final message can never map to exit 0. (IT-3, REG-2)
- **AC5** — On retry exhaustion in interactive mode the run prints the error and returns to the prompt; the session stays alive and steerable. (IT-4)
- **AC6** — Reasoning-only completions (thinking deltas, no text) that carry tool calls are never classified as empty and never trigger the retry path. (UT-5, E4)
- **AC7** — A model that persistently returns empty (hiccup storm) terminates the run after exactly N retries — no retry storm, no unbounded loop, deterministic attempt count. (IT-2, E3)

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero regression on the #1085 settle semantics

- **UT-1** (pure, no IO): `classifyEmptyCompletion` — empty message after partial text in turn → `emptyAfterPartial`. Maps AC1.
- **UT-2**: empty message after previous message with `StopReason.length` and after one with the silent-truncation `errorMessage` flag → `emptyAfterPartial`. Maps AC1.
- **UT-3**: empty message, no prior partial content, clean stop → `cleanEmpty`; budget/budget-exhausted branches of `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` unchanged. Maps AC2.
- **UT-4**: retry policy — attempt count capped at N, backoff sequence computed, `CancelToken` cancelled between attempts suppresses the next attempt. Maps AC3.
- **UT-5**: content classification — thinking-only + `ToolCall` → not empty; thinking-only, no text, no tool calls → empty; whitespace-only text → empty. Maps AC6.
- **IT-1** (fake `StreamFunction` / mock LLM, deterministic): scripted sequence `partial text stream → empty completion → healthy completion` — the agent retries and finishes the task; assert the run's final exit outcome is success and the retried empties are in the transcript. Maps AC1, AC3.
- **IT-2**: scripted `partial → empty × (N+1)` — exactly N retries fire (no storm), then exhaustion verdict. Maps AC3, AC7, E3.
- **IT-3**: headless `-p` run driven to exhaustion — process exit code is non-zero, stderr carries the error line naming attempts and last stop reason. Maps AC4, REG-2.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # #1368: the publish job consumes dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict
    # — instead of this aggregate's result. The aggregate itself stays the
    # single required check: any red leg (platform included) still fails it.
    outputs:
      dart_ok: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.dart_ok }}
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-analyze = ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "usage-fold    = ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "fa-aot-build  = ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
          echo "pin-gate    = ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}"
          echo "exzone      = ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}"
          echo "lock-smoke  = ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        id: gate

          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_USAGE_FOLD: ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_FA_AOT: ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE: ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}
          R_EXZONE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}
          R_LOCK_SMOKE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
          dart_blocker=""
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.

          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          # #1368 — two independent verdicts over the needs legs:
          #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
          #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
          #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
          #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
          #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,

                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "fa-aot-build:$R_FA_AOT" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \

content.text:
# leg merged INTO the linux leg below — ONE sharded PTY/CLI integration
  # job on ubuntu-24.04-arm that now also carries the per-shard coverage +
  # dart-json/junit reporting the gate consumes. A PR validation's PTY legs
  # never wait on fa-m5-1; hosted macOS (10x minute cost) is never used.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  pty-integration-linux:
    # THE PR PTY/CLI integration leg (gh-1005: the former mac leg merged in;
    # before that, issue #931 part 2 sharded ONE ~40-min job into 3
    # duration-balanced shards — scripts/test_integration_shards.json,
    # file-level units). New integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the rate-limit rationale is
    # documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    # gh-1300: needs the once-per-run AOT build; FA_BIN points every CLI
    # spawn (PTY harness + headless helpers) at the prebuilt binary.
    needs: [release-pending, fa-aot-build]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    name: PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    # 40 > 30: the leg now carries the coverage + file-reporter overhead the
    # old mac leg had (the coverage-free linux twin never paid it) and arm64
    # Graviton cores run somewhat slower than the M-series minis did — margin
    # without stretching the watchdog much.
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # Secret shape (review 2026-09-23): this is the pull_request-time leg
      # that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds secrets from
      # forks, so external contributions never see them — but every
      # SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — lower-numbered — value; missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully and the gate stays honest either
      # way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # gh-1300: the AOT binary built once per run by fa-aot-build. The
      # guard FAILS the shard loudly if the artifact is missing or dead —
      # a silent JIT fallback would hide the optimization from AC1's
      # before/after numbers.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/release_hygiene_test.dart pins the pin).
      #
      # gh-1412: each evidence upload carries a one-shot retry (the step
      # right after it, same pinned action). The gh-1412 validation run
      # 37807820733 red'd a shard whose 68 tests ALL passed on a single
      # transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET` from GitHub's
      # blob storage — the aggregate gate followed and the merge aborted.
      # The retry re-runs the SAME action with overwrite:true (a failed
      # attempt leaves the artifact half-registered — without overwrite the
      # retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely dead endpoint still
      # fails the shard loudly, and the retries stay if: always()-reachable
      # so red legs keep their evidence. Guarded by
      # test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        id: upload_integration_json
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1582
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1582
- **Title**: gh-1577 [GOAL] Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0 (B2)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1577` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1338
- **Deletions**: -69
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T10:03:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T19:39:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1577
## gh-1577 — Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0

### What changed
- An empty assistant completion that follows partial content (assistant text, tool activity, or a truncation signal earlier in the turn) is now a **bounded-retry provider hiccup** in the agent loop; on retry exhaustion the run ends with a loud `StopReason.error` naming the hiccup, attempt count and last stop reason — headless `-p` exits 1, interactive prints the error and returns to the prompt. The silent exit-0 settle is gone.
- A clean empty (no partial content anywhere in the turn) keeps the #1085 M2b semantics exactly: one `continue` nudge per logical turn, then settle.

### Key decisions
- New pure classifier `classifyEmptyCompletion(turnHistory, message)` (`lib/src/agent/empty_completion.dart`) with verdicts `notEmpty` / `emptyAfterPartial` / `cleanEmpty` / `abortedOrError` — shared by the loop's retry machinery and the CLI's nudge gate; the partial-content window is the TURN (messages after the last user message), so an old truncation can never resurrect retries (E1).
- Truncation signals: `StopReason.length` plus the tolerated silent-truncation `errorMessage` flag count as partial-context evidence (E6); the `ToolCall` boundary survives — thinking-only turns with tool calls are never empty (AC6/E4).
- Retry policy lives in the loop (`agent_loop_empty_completion.dart`, a `part of agent_loop.dart` to stay under the 2800-line gate): `emptyHiccupRetries` (default 3, knob alongside `maxEmptyRetries`), exponential backoff in the model-roles `retry.baseDelayMs`/`maxBackoffMs` shape (500ms → 8s cap, deterministic), re-streamed through `_streamAssistantResponse`; retried empties stay in the transcript. `CancelToken` is honored between attempts; an abort racing the classification settles `aborted` (exit 130) — never the hiccup error, never a silent empty (E2/E5).
- Exhaustion reuses `StopReason.error` (open question 2) — the existing headless exit-code switch maps it to 1 with no switch change; the legacy `maxEmptyRetries` budget and the CLI's `maxEmptyRetries: 0` wiring are untouched.
- REG-2 scope note: the never-exit-0 contract is enforced for the hiccup family (empty after partial content) across the `stop` / length-flagged / silent-truncation-flagged paths; the clean-empty settle after its one nudge keeps AC2's pinned exit-0 behavior (REG-1).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/empty_completion_test.dart test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart
dart test --exclude-tags integration   # full gate suite
```

### Test coverage
- UT-1..UT-5: classifier verdicts incl. thinking+ToolCall not empty, whitespace-only empty, backoff sequence.
- IT-1: `partial → empty → healthy` recovers and finishes (exit 0, retried empty in transcript). IT-2/E3: `partial → empty ×(N+1)` fires exactly N retries then the loud error. IT-3/REG-2: headless exhaustion exits 1 across all stop-reason variants. IT-4/AC5: interactive exhaustion returns to a steerable prompt. REG-1: clean-empty one-nudge tests unchanged.
- UT/IT run in the default CI shard (files verified bin-packed by `shard_files.py`); E2E-1 (live provider lane) and the REG required-check job wiring are CI-config follow-ups, no code dependency.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[assistant completion] --> C{classifyEmptyCompletion}
  C -->|notEmpty / abortedOrError| OWN[existing terminal paths]
  C -->|cleanEmpty| NUDGE[one continue nudge, then settle - #1085 M2b unchanged]
  C -->|emptyAfterPartial| R[bounded retry: N=3, backoff 500ms to 8s]
  R -->|healthy| RUN[turn continues]
  R -->|cancel| AB[settle aborted - exit 130]
  R -->|N retries spent, still empty| ERR[StopReason.error naming hiccup + attempts + last stop]
  ERR -->|headless -p| X1[exit 1]
  ERR -->|interactive| P[error line + prompt stays alive]
```
</details>

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: gh-1577's core fix is solid — the shared classifier, bounded backoff retry, loud exhaustion verdict and preserved #1085 M2b clean-empty semantics all check out (analyzer clean, all 71 tests in the three new/extended suites pass, both new test files are runtime bin-packed into the CI shards, `agent_loop.dart` stays under the 2800-line gate). One blocking correctness leak remains: an abort racing the last retry can still settle headless as exit 0 when the final empty is truncation-flagged.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 BLOCKING — `agent_loop_empty_completion.dart:89`: the E5 abort conversion only covers `StopReason.stop` empties; a cancel/deadline abort landing while the final retry returns a length-flagged or silent-truncation-flagged empty escapes the loop and settles exit 0 (a regression vs `main`, where the nudge path converted it to aborted/130).
- ⚠️ `agent_loop.dart:490`: doc claims `emptyHiccupRetries: 0` "restores the legacy accept-empty settle" — it actually produces the exhaustion error; no config restores the legacy settle.
- ⚠️ `agent_loop.dart:491`: the knobs stop at `AgentLoopConfig` — `Agent` facade and `AgentWiringSpec` (the CLI/host seam, where `maxEmptyRetries` lives) can't tune them, so AC3's "configurable N" is unreachable for the CLI and the new CLI tests sleep ~14s of real backoff per run.
- 💡 Backoff sleep ignores cancellation (up to 8s dead window after Ctrl+C).

**Ticket notes**: REG-2 is deliberately narrowed to the hiccup family — a clean empty still settles exit 0 after its one nudge (AC2/REG-1); the ticket's invariant 1 and AC2 are mutually contradictory and the PR resolves in favor of AC2 — worth an owner sign-off. E2E-1 and the REG required-check CI wiring remain declared follow-ups; E7 deadline-aware backoff is not implemented (deadline aborts cut retries via the token, modulo the blocking race above).

**Next Steps**:
1. Broaden the E5 post-loop conversion to any empty (`isEmptyAssistantCompletion`) so the abort always wins.
2. Fix the `emptyHiccupRetries: 0` doc to match the implemented (correct) behavior.
3. Thread the three hiccup knobs through `AgentConfig`/`AgentWiringSpec` next to `maxEmptyRetries`; zero the backoff in the CLI tests.

### Thread 7

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-13):

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-13):

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-13):

🚨 **BLOCKING: abort can still settle as exit 0 when the last retry returns a truncation-flagged empty (E2/E5 leak)**

The E5 conversion only covers *clean-stop* empties — `_isDegenerateEmpty` requires `StopReason.stop`:

```dart
if (cancelled && _isDegenerateEmpty(current)) {
  current = await _finishWithoutStream(
    out,
    emit,
    _terminalMessage(config.model, StopReason.aborted, 'Operation aborted'),
  );
}
```

Race: the cancel token fires while the final hiccup retry is in flight and the provider answers with an empty that is `StopReason.length` or silent-truncation-flagged (`stop` + `errorMessage`). The loop exits via `!cancelled`, the post-check is false (stop reason is `length`, not `stop`), and the empty message escapes the loop as a normal final → `_terminalRunMessages` returns null → the turn settles → headless exit **0** on an aborted run.

This is also a regression vs `main`: the old `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` (`stopReason != error && != aborted && empty`) nudged those variants, and the nudged run short-circuited in `_streamAssistantResponse` → `_abortedTurn` → exit 130. The new `cleanEmpty`-only gate removed that accidental recovery.

Deadline-abort landing in this window converts a killed session into a false success — exactly the gh-1577 failure class this PR exists to kill. Fix is one line — let the abort win for *any* empty:

```dart
if (cancelled && isEmptyAssistantCompletion(current)) {
  ...
}
```

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-13):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the `emptyHiccupRetries: 0` doc promises an escape hatch that does not exist**

`AgentLoopConfig.emptyHiccupRetries` docs say: *"Default: 3. `0` restores the legacy accept-empty settle."* Tracing `retryEmptyCompletion` with `0`:

- CLI shape (`maxEmptyRetries: 0`): iteration 1 on an `emptyAfterPartial` → generic budget spent (0 not < 0) → not `cleanEmpty` → `hiccup (0) >= 0` → immediate exhaustion `StopReason.error`.
- App-host shape (`maxEmptyRetries: 1`): one silent generic retry, then the exhaustion error.

No configuration restores the legacy accept-empty settle for the hiccup family. The implemented behavior is arguably the *right* one (the ticket's contract is "never a silent exit 0"), so please fix the doc rather than the code — as written, an operator setting `0` to opt out of the new contract gets a loud run error instead of the documented legacy settle.

# gh-1577: [GOAL] Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0 (B2)

## Description

## Goal — truncated-stream + empty-completion never settles a run as success (v1, initial filing)

One sentence: **an empty assistant completion that follows partial/truncated content becomes a bounded-retry provider hiccup and, on exhaustion, a loud run error — never a silent exit 0** — instead of the one-shot "continue" nudge settling the run as a clean final answer.

Today the CLI treats every empty assistant message alike: `_noteQuietMessageEnd` prints `(empty response: the model returned no text — it may be rate-limited or reasoning-only)` and `_settleAfterPrompt` fires exactly ONE `continue` nudge per logical turn (`_emptyReplyNudgesLeft = 1`, reset in `_beginUserPrompt`). When the second consecutive reply is also empty, the turn settles with `StopReason.stop`, the headless exit-code switch maps it to `0`, and the session dies mid-task. Verified on TB 2.1 artifacts (run 38271607849, `circuit-fibsqrt__{HdcYpf3,jmMMKVo,g2Bt7AT}/agent/fa.txt`): the model's text truncates mid-code (`unsigned long long N = strtoull(argv[1`), the next completion returns empty, the nudge budget is already spent, and the process exits `__FA_EXIT=0` with ~54 minutes left to the session deadline, `gates.txt` unwritten, reward 0 — 3 of 5 trials of one task killed by this path (task score 2/5 instead of a possible 5/5).

## Why this framing

- This is a **run-outcome classification** bug, not a rendering bug: the note text is honest, the exit code is the lie. Earlier adjacent work (#413: exit code from turn events, not transcript; #1085 M2b: one nudge per logical turn) fixed compaction-masking and infinite-loop risks; this card fixes the remaining false-positive class — *truncated stream followed by an empty completion read as an intentional final answer*.
- The fix targets the **agent-loop / settle layer**, not the provider clients: the hiccup signature (partial content earlier in the turn → empty completion now) is visible only where turn history and stop reasons meet.

## Architecture

Named components, all existing:

- **Degenerate-empty classifier** — extend `_isDegenerateEmpty` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`) and `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart`) into a single classification function `classifyEmptyCompletion(turnHistory, message)` with three verdicts:
  - `emptyAfterPartial` — the turn already contains non-whitespace assistant text or tool activity, OR the previous assistant message carried a truncation signal (`StopReason.length`, or the tolerated-silent-truncation `errorMessage` flag), and the new completion is empty. Verdict: **retryable hiccup**.
  - `cleanEmpty` — no partial content anywhere in the turn, clean `stop`: a genuine empty final. Verdict: existing single-nudge behavior, unchanged.
  - `abortedOrError` — `StopReason.aborted`/`error`: never classified as empty (today's guard, kept).
- **Bounded retry policy for `emptyAfterPartial`** — N retries (default 3, config key alongside `maxEmptyRetries`) with exponential backoff (reuse the `retriesPerEntry`/`baseDelayMs`/`maxBackoffMs` shape from `lib/src/model_roles/roles_config.dart`); each retry is re-streamed through `_streamAssistantResponse`; `CancelToken` is honored between attempts (no new request after cancel).
- **Exhaustion verdict** — when retries are spent and the completion is still empty: the run ends with an explicit **run error** (loud error line naming the hiccup, attempt count, and last stop reason), NOT a quiet settle. Headless (`-p`): the terminal stop reason surfaces as `StopReason.error` → exit code 1 (the existing switch at `agent_cli.dart` maps it — extend it if a dedicated stop reason is introduced). Interactive TUI/REPL: the error line plus return to prompt — the user steers; the session is never silently closed.
- Invariants: (1) headless exit 0 requires at least one non-empty assistant message or executed tool call in the run's final turn; (2) a retry never fires after user/harness abort; (3) retried empty messages stay in the transcript (truthful record, as `_retryDegenerateEmpty` already documents); (4) reasoning-only turns (thinking content but no text) WITH tool calls are never classified empty — today's `ToolCall` check in `_assistantMessageIsEmpty` is the boundary and must survive.

## Capability surface

| Surface | Core (this card) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `emptyAfterPartial` detection | yes | partial = prior text/tool activity in turn OR truncation stop reason/flag on previous message |
| Bounded backoff retry (headless `-p`) | yes | default N=3, configurable; backoff per retry-policy shape |
| Run-error on exhaustion (headless: exit ≠ 0) | yes | exit-code contract: empty-finish never 0 without content |
| Interactive TUI: error + prompt instead of silent settle | yes | same classification, UX is steer/prompt |
| `cleanEmpty` single-nudge | unchanged | issue #1085 M2b semantics preserved |
| Second tier (opt-in follow-up) | — | surface retry events in trajectory view / fa.log structured fields; metric counter for hiccup rate per provider |
| Excluded | provider-client changes | the hiccup is classified at loop level; no HTTP-layer changes — rationale: truncation signature spans messages, invisible to the client |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — An empty completion immediately following a turn that produced partial assistant text (or whose previous message ended `StopReason.length` / silent-truncation-flagged) is classified `emptyAfterPartial` and triggers a bounded retry, not the one-shot nudge and not a settle. (UT-1, UT-2, IT-1)
- **AC2** — A clean empty completion with no partial content anywhere in the turn keeps today's behavior exactly: one `continue` nudge per logical turn, then settle. (UT-3, REG-1)
- **AC3** — Retries are bounded (configurable N, default 3) with backoff; each attempt respects cancellation; no retry is issued after an abort. (UT-4, IT-2, E2)
- **AC4** — On retry exhaustion in headless `-p` mode the process exits non-zero with a loud error line; the empty final message can never map to exit 0. (IT-3, REG-2)
- **AC5** — On retry exhaustion in interactive mode the run prints the error and returns to the prompt; the session stays alive and steerable. (IT-4)
- **AC6** — Reasoning-only completions (thinking deltas, no text) that carry tool calls are never classified as empty and never trigger the retry path. (UT-5, E4)
- **AC7** — A model that persistently returns empty (hiccup storm) terminates the run after exactly N retries — no retry storm, no unbounded loop, deterministic attempt count. (IT-2, E3)

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero regression on the #1085 settle semantics

- **UT-1** (pure, no IO): `classifyEmptyCompletion` — empty message after partial text in turn → `emptyAfterPartial`. Maps AC1.
- **UT-2**: empty message after previous message with `StopReason.length` and after one with the silent-truncation `errorMessage` flag → `emptyAfterPartial`. Maps AC1.
- **UT-3**: empty message, no prior partial content, clean stop → `cleanEmpty`; budget/budget-exhausted branches of `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` unchanged. Maps AC2.
- **UT-4**: retry policy — attempt count capped at N, backoff sequence computed, `CancelToken` cancelled between attempts suppresses the next attempt. Maps AC3.
- **UT-5**: content classification — thinking-only + `ToolCall` → not empty; thinking-only, no text, no tool calls → empty; whitespace-only text → empty. Maps AC6.
- **IT-1** (fake `StreamFunction` / mock LLM, deterministic): scripted sequence `partial text stream → empty completion → healthy completion` — the agent retries and finishes the task; assert the run's final exit outcome is success and the retried empties are in the transcript. Maps AC1, AC3.
- **IT-2**: scripted `partial → empty × (N+1)` — exactly N retries fire (no storm), then exhaustion verdict. Maps AC3, AC7, E3.
- **IT-3**: headless `-p` run driven to exhaustion — process exit code is non-zero, stderr carries the error line naming attempts and last stop reason. Maps AC4, REG-2.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

blocks.text:
# leg merged INTO the linux leg below — ONE sharded PTY/CLI integration
  # job on ubuntu-24.04-arm that now also carries the per-shard coverage +
  # dart-json/junit reporting the gate consumes. A PR validation's PTY legs
  # never wait on fa-m5-1; hosted macOS (10x minute cost) is never used.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  pty-integration-linux:
    # THE PR PTY/CLI integration leg (gh-1005: the former mac leg merged in;
    # before that, issue #931 part 2 sharded ONE ~40-min job into 3
    # duration-balanced shards — scripts/test_integration_shards.json,
    # file-level units). New integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the rate-limit rationale is
    # documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    # gh-1300: needs the once-per-run AOT build; FA_BIN points every CLI
    # spawn (PTY harness + headless helpers) at the prebuilt binary.
    needs: [release-pending, fa-aot-build]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    name: PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    # 40 > 30: the leg now carries the coverage + file-reporter overhead the
    # old mac leg had (the coverage-free linux twin never paid it) and arm64
    # Graviton cores run somewhat slower than the M-series minis did — margin
    # without stretching the watchdog much.
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # Secret shape (review 2026-09-23): this is the pull_request-time leg
      # that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds secrets from
      # forks, so external contributions never see them — but every
      # SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — lower-numbered — value; missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully and the gate stays honest either
      # way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # gh-1300: the AOT binary built once per run by fa-aot-build. The
      # guard FAILS the shard loudly if the artifact is missing or dead —
      # a silent JIT fallback would hide the optimization from AC1's
      # before/after numbers.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-ar…
