blocks.text:
# leg merged INTO the linux leg below — ONE sharded PTY/CLI integration
  # job on ubuntu-24.04-arm that now also carries the per-shard coverage +
  # dart-json/junit reporting the gate consumes. A PR validation's PTY legs
  # never wait on fa-m5-1; hosted macOS (10x minute cost) is never used.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  pty-integration-linux:
    # THE PR PTY/CLI integration leg (gh-1005: the former mac leg merged in;
    # before that, issue #931 part 2 sharded ONE ~40-min job into 3
    # duration-balanced shards — scripts/test_integration_shards.json,
    # file-level units). New integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the rate-limit rationale is
    # documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    # gh-1300: needs the once-per-run AOT build; FA_BIN points every CLI
    # spawn (PTY harness + headless helpers) at the prebuilt binary.
    needs: [release-pending, fa-aot-build]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    name: PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    # 40 > 30: the leg now carries the coverage + file-reporter overhead the
    # old mac leg had (the coverage-free linux twin never paid it) and arm64
    # Graviton cores run somewhat slower than the M-series minis did — margin
    # without stretching the watchdog much.
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # Secret shape (review 2026-09-23): this is the pull_request-time leg
      # that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds secrets from
      # forks, so external contributions never see them — but every
      # SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — lower-numbered — value; missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully and the gate stays honest either
      # way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # gh-1300: the AOT binary built once per run by fa-aot-build. The
      # guard FAILS the shard loudly if the artifact is missing or dead —
      # a silent JIT fallback would hide the optimization from AC1's
      # before/after numbers.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-ar…

# leg merged INTO the linux leg below — ONE sharded PTY/CLI integration
  # job on ubuntu-24.04-arm that now also carries the per-shard coverage +
  # dart-json/junit reporting the gate consumes. A PR validation's PTY legs
  # never wait on fa-m5-1; hosted macOS (10x minute cost) is never used.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  pty-integration-linux:
    # THE PR PTY/CLI integration leg (gh-1005: the former mac leg merged in;
    # before that, issue #931 part 2 sharded ONE ~40-min job into 3
    # duration-balanced shards — scripts/test_integration_shards.json,
    # file-level units). New integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the rate-limit rationale is
    # documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    # gh-1300: needs the once-per-run AOT build; FA_BIN points every CLI
    # spawn (PTY harness + headless helpers) at the prebuilt binary.
    needs: [release-pending, fa-aot-build]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    name: PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    # 40 > 30: the leg now carries the coverage + file-reporter overhead the
    # old mac leg had (the coverage-free linux twin never paid it) and arm64
    # Graviton cores run somewhat slower than the M-series minis did — margin
    # without stretching the watchdog much.
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # Secret shape (review 2026-09-23): this is the pull_request-time leg
      # that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds secrets from
      # forks, so external contributions never see them — but every
      # SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — lower-numbered — value; missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully and the gate stays honest either
      # way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # gh-1300: the AOT binary built once per run by fa-aot-build. The
      # guard FAILS the shard loudly if the artifact is missing or dead —
      # a silent JIT fallback would hide the optimization from AC1's
      # before/after numbers.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-ar…

quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # #1368: the publish job consumes dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict
    # — instead of this aggregate's result. The aggregate itself stays the
    # single required check: any red leg (platform included) still fails it.
    outputs:
      dart_ok: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.dart_ok }}
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-analyze = ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "usage-fold    = ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "fa-aot-build  = ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
          echo "pin-gate    = ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}"
          echo "exzone      = ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}"
          echo "lock-smoke  = ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        id: gate
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_USAGE_FOLD: ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_FA_AOT: ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE: ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}
          R_EXZONE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}
          R_LOCK_SMOKE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
          dart_blocker=""
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then

          fi
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then

                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "fa-aot-build:$R_FA_AOT" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \
                    "flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE" "flutter-app-lock-smoke:$R_LOCK_SMOKE"; do

# leg merged INTO the linux leg below — ONE sharded PTY/CLI integration
  # job on ubuntu-24.04-arm that now also carries the per-shard coverage +
  # dart-json/junit reporting the gate consumes. A PR validation's PTY legs
  # never wait on fa-m5-1; hosted macOS (10x minute cost) is never used.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  pty-integration-linux:
    # THE PR PTY/CLI integration leg (gh-1005: the former mac leg merged in;
    # before that, issue #931 part 2 sharded ONE ~40-min job into 3
    # duration-balanced shards — scripts/test_integration_shards.json,
    # file-level units). New integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the rate-limit rationale is
    # documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    # gh-1300: needs the once-per-run AOT build; FA_BIN points every CLI
    # spawn (PTY harness + headless helpers) at the prebuilt binary.
    needs: [release-pending, fa-aot-build]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    name: PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    # 40 > 30: the leg now carries the coverage + file-reporter overhead the
    # old mac leg had (the coverage-free linux twin never paid it) and arm64
    # Graviton cores run somewhat slower than the M-series minis did — margin
    # without stretching the watchdog much.
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # Secret shape (review 2026-09-23): this is the pull_request-time leg
      # that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds secrets from
      # forks, so external contributions never see them — but every
      # SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — lower-numbered — value; missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully and the gate stays honest either
      # way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # gh-1300: the AOT binary built once per run by fa-aot-build. The
      # guard FAILS the shard loudly if the artifact is missing or dead —
      # a silent JIT fallback would hide the optimization from AC1's
      # before/after numbers.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the

# leg merged INTO the linux leg below — ONE sharded PTY/CLI integration
  # job on ubuntu-24.04-arm that now also carries the per-shard coverage +
  # dart-json/junit reporting the gate consumes. A PR validation's PTY legs
  # never wait on fa-m5-1; hosted macOS (10x minute cost) is never used.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  pty-integration-linux:
    # THE PR PTY/CLI integration leg (gh-1005: the former mac leg merged in;
    # before that, issue #931 part 2 sharded ONE ~40-min job into 3
    # duration-balanced shards — scripts/test_integration_shards.json,
    # file-level units). New integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the rate-limit rationale is
    # documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    # gh-1300: needs the once-per-run AOT build; FA_BIN points every CLI
    # spawn (PTY harness + headless helpers) at the prebuilt binary.
    needs: [release-pending, fa-aot-build]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    name: PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    # 40 > 30: the leg now carries the coverage + file-reporter overhead the
    # old mac leg had (the coverage-free linux twin never paid it) and arm64
    # Graviton cores run somewhat slower than the M-series minis did — margin
    # without stretching the watchdog much.
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # Secret shape (review 2026-09-23): this is the pull_request-time leg
      # that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds secrets from
      # forks, so external contributions never see them — but every
      # SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — lower-numbered — value; missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully and the gate stays honest either
      # way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # gh-1300: the AOT binary built once per run by fa-aot-build. The
      # guard FAILS the shard loudly if the artifact is missing or dead —
      # a silent JIT fallback would hide the optimization from AC1's
      # before/after numbers.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the

# leg merged INTO the linux leg below — ONE sharded PTY/CLI integration
  # job on ubuntu-24.04-arm that now also carries the per-shard coverage +
  # dart-json/junit reporting the gate consumes. A PR validation's PTY legs
  # never wait on fa-m5-1; hosted macOS (10x minute cost) is never used.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  pty-integration-linux:
    # THE PR PTY/CLI integration leg (gh-1005: the former mac leg merged in;
    # before that, issue #931 part 2 sharded ONE ~40-min job into 3
    # duration-balanced shards — scripts/test_integration_shards.json,
    # file-level units). New integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the rate-limit rationale is
    # documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    # gh-1300: needs the once-per-run AOT build; FA_BIN points every CLI
    # spawn (PTY harness + headless helpers) at the prebuilt binary.
    needs: [release-pending, fa-aot-build]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    name: PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    # 40 > 30: the leg now carries the coverage + file-reporter overhead the
    # old mac leg had (the coverage-free linux twin never paid it) and arm64
    # Graviton cores run somewhat slower than the M-series minis did — margin
    # without stretching the watchdog much.
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # Secret shape (review 2026-09-23): this is the pull_request-time leg
      # that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds secrets from
      # forks, so external contributions never see them — but every
      # SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — lower-numbered — value; missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully and the gate stays honest either
      # way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # gh-1300: the AOT binary built once per run by fa-aot-build. The
      # guard FAILS the shard loudly if the artifact is missing or dead —
      # a silent JIT fallback would hide the optimization from AC1's
      # before/after numbers.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.

          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)

          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the

If the loop had received the chunk, tokens would be > 0? Not necessarily — the token counter may only update at message finalize. But "Working… 59s" means the turn never finished.

Hmm, one candidate mechanism connecting to this PR: the loop's `_streamAssistantResponse` short-circuit on cancel? No cancel here.

Another: the CLI `emptyHiccupBaseDelay` default is 500ms — only used between hiccup retries of EMPTY completions. The echo mock returns non-empty.

What about the boot? The session was booted, config written with `mode: code`... The run started at "19:30:55" (session dir name 2026-10-13T19-30-55). The shard started tests ~19:30. The timeout fired at 19:31:57 = 62s later. Working… 59s.

Wait, actually — let me look again at the screen: the composer shows "gate-echo-marker" in row 15, and the status "Working… 59s · submit". Hmm, and the raw tail shows the composer GRID being painted (the 10-50 column numbers) — that's the TUI composer wrap grid rendered at [20;30H etc.

Interesting: in the raw tail, "Working… 0s · submit" appears — the run JUST started when that frame was painted. Then the poll waited 60s and the screen still showed "Working… 59s". So the run was genuinely working for 59s with no reply.

The mock is in-process with the test (HttpServer bound to 127.0.0.1). The AOT binary connects to 127.0.0.1:45761. The mock received the request? If the request had arrived, the mock would respond in ms. If the request never arrived (connect failed?), the provider watchdog (providerConnectTimeout 180s) would hold... The CLI waits on the connect timeout of 180s! The screen would show Working for a long time. But the test's waitForText budget is 30s (×2 = 60s) → TimeoutException.

So the failure = the provider request never completed within 60s. Connect timeout is 180s; so if the TCP connect silently failed or the endpoint was unreachable, the CLI would hang in Working until 180s — past the test budget.

Why would 127.0.0.1 connect fail/hang in CI? The mock listens inside the test process. On the arm runner, with concurrency=4... Hmm. Actually the request could have been sent and the response never parsed? Or the TUI never rendered?

Honestly this smells like an infra flake on the loaded arm runner (multiple concurrent shards, AOT spawn ~1s, PTY timing). The repo has a documented flake problem (branch 1026-flaky-pty-timing...). And there's a quarantine mechanism: scripts/test_quarantine.json — flaky tests get quarantined pending fixes.

The repo has an established flake-quarantine mechanism: a PTY test that flakes in the gate gets quarantined (removed from deterministic legs) pending a fix, with a tracker issue and ≥2 distinct failing SHAs as proof.

The `ssh_shift_gate_test.dart` is not quarantined — but it may have just started flaking. Before quarantining (which is a workflow/manifest change and might beyond my remit), let me gather evidence:

1. Check if this test failed in OTHER recent CI runs (other branches) — the runs list shows many red runs today; let me check a few more pty legs from other branches to see if ssh_shift_gate failed there too. 

Actually, the runs I listed with status=failure only show one failing leg each. For runs on OTHER branches where pty-integration-linux passed, ssh_shift_gate passed. The question is whether ssh_shift_gate flaked elsewhere recently.

Let me look at the flake-watch tooling and recent nightly data. Actually — simpler: let me check the last ~20 pty-integration-linux job results on all branches and grep for ssh_shift_gate failures. That's a lot of API calls. Alternative: the flake_watch.py script probably reads test-results artifacts.

Alternatively, run the failing test repeatedly locally to see if it's reproducibly flaky under load. And also run the OTHER PTY tests in shard 2 that exercise similar paths.

Actually, wait. Let me think about the failure more carefully. A key detail in the log: the failing run was at 19:30-19:31. The whole shard ran from 19:30:04 to 19:32:00 — under 2 minutes for 112 tests?? Look: the first step timestamps: 19:30:04 runner provision, dart test started ~19:30:30?, failed test at 19:31:57, and the summary "111 tests passed, 1 failed" at 19:32:00. That's a very fast shard — plausible with concurrency=4 and the AOT binary (~1s per spawn).

Hmm wait, actually that seems too fast for 112 integration tests including perf_open_gate (3.7s) etc. But it's arm64 with concurrency 4. Plausible.

Now, the specific failure: "TimeoutException after 0:01:00.000: Timed out waiting for gate-echo-marker-reply in output." — the harness's waitForText budget was 60s (30s × FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2). The screen showed "Working… 59s · submit".

So the CLI was working for 59s. The mock should answer instantly. Unless the request never reached the mock, OR the request reached the mock but the response was never processed, OR the CLI was stuck somewhere else entirely (e.g., the shift-HID poll! — this test is about the SSH gate: with SSH env, the Shift+Enter HID polling is disabled. The failure is in the FIRST phase: submit + reply).

Hmm wait, actually, let me reconsider: "Working… 59s" — the elapsed counter counts from submit. If the provider request hung on connect... to 127.0.0.1 — that can't hang on connect normally (localhost either connects or refuses). Unless the arm runner's loopback was saturated.

OR: the response arrived but the model's reply was classified EMPTY and the loop retried with backoff — 500ms+1s+2s+4s = 7.5s, then exhaustion error. That would end the turn in ~8s, not 59s.

OR: the completion arrived, and the turn continued into a TOOL call loop? The echo reply is "gate-echo-marker-reply" — no tool calls. 

OR the AOT binary failed to boot and the harness's waitForBoot passed on some early output, then the submit went nowhere. But the screen shows the full TUI booted (session path, model, endpoint). And the submitted message shows in the transcript row 15 " gate-echo-marker". The status "Working… 59s" means the run began.

So: request sent → no response processed for 59s. On an overloaded arm runner with 4 concurrent tests each spawning AOT CLI processes... the mock server is IN the test process — if the test process's event loop was busy (the harness polls the PTY screen with regex over ANSI output every X ms), the HttpServer might be starved? The test process runs pollUntil which awaits streams — the event loop stays live. The mock should still answer.

Unless the RESPONSE was answered but the SSE parsing on the CLI side didn't complete because the connection stayed open... the mock closes the response after [DONE]. Fine.

OK — I can't fully diagnose a timing flake from one artifact. Evidence so far:
1. Test passes locally (JIT).
2. Broad CI redness today across many branches, including main and release tags, on DIFFERENT legs (flutter app tests shard 0/2 on main, PTY here). 
3. The repo's PTY suite has a documented flake problem with a formal quarantine process.

Let me now check the shard's dart-test json artifact for the failing run — the per-test durations might show resource starvation (all tests slow). Also check whether OTHER ssh_shift_gate tests passed in the same shard ("FA_TUI_SHIFT_HID=0 without SSH env" PASSED in the same CI run — same mock, same spawn path, only the SSH env differs!). That's important: the second test in the SAME file with the SAME mock passed right after. So mock + spawn + submit + reply worked fine at 19:31:58. The difference: SSH_CONNECTION/SSH_TTY env vars → the shift-HID gate.

So the first test failed waiting for the REPLY — but the second test's reply came through fine seconds later. The reply path (mock→CLI→render) works. So in the failed test, either the submit didn't trigger a request, or the request/response raced.

Hmm — the SSH gate disables the HID poll. The submit path: sendText('gate-echo-marker') then sendEnter(). With SSH env, Enter submits (that's the test's assertion). If the Enter was eaten (PTY timing), the composer would still show the text and nothing would run — but the screen shows "Working… 59s", so the run DID start. The run started but never produced the reply.

Actually wait, let me look at the raw tail once more: "Working… 0s · submit" then the composer grid painting. The status row shows "Working… 0s" — at that frame the run had just started. Then nothing for 59s.

Hmm, what about this: the reply DID arrive and the run finished, but the transcript rendering of the reply happened... the screen at timeout shows "Working… 59s" — the status row says still Working at 59s. So the run genuinely hadn't finished at 59s.

A 59s hang in Working with a local mock. Connect timeout is 180s — if the request was never sent (queued behind something) or the socket connect blocked...

What in this PR could delay the FIRST request? Let me look at the full agent_loop diff for the streaming path. If e.g. the retry machinery wraps the stream call in a way that could stall... Let me read agent_loop_empty_completion.dart fully, plus the loop changes in agent_loop.dart.

The second test in the same file (same mock, same spawn, no SSH env) passed right after — so the mock and spawn path work. Let me study the loop diff for anything that could stall the first request, and check the per-test durations in the CI artifact.

The `ssh_shift_gate_test.dart` is not quarantined — but it may have just started flaking. Before quarantining (which is a workflow/manifest change and might beyond my remit), let me gather evidence:

1. Check if this test failed in OTHER recent CI runs (other branches) — the runs list shows many red runs today; let me check a few more pty legs from other branches to see if ssh_shift_gate failed there too. 

Actually, the runs I listed with status=failure only show one failing leg each. For runs on OTHER branches where pty-integration-linux passed, ssh_shift_gate passed. The question is whether ssh_shift_gate flaked elsewhere recently.

Let me look at the flake-watch tooling and recent nightly data. Actually — simpler: let me check the last ~20 pty-integration-linux job results on all branches and grep for ssh_shift_gate failures. That's a lot of API calls. Alternative: the flake_watch.py script probably reads test-results artifacts.

Alternatively, run the failing test repeatedly locally to see if it's reproducibly flaky under load. And also run the OTHER PTY tests in shard 2 that exercise similar paths.

Actually, wait. Let me think about the failure more carefully. A key detail in the log: the failing run was at 19:30-19:31. The whole shard ran from 19:30:04 to 19:32:00 — under 2 minutes for 112 tests?? Look: the first step timestamps: 19:30:04 runner provision, dart test started ~19:30:30?, failed test at 19:31:57, and the summary "111 tests passed, 1 failed" at 19:32:00. That's a very fast shard — plausible with concurrency=4 and the AOT binary (~1s per spawn).

Hmm wait, actually that seems too fast for 112 integration tests including perf_open_gate (3.7s) etc. But it's arm64 with concurrency 4. Plausible.

Now, the specific failure: "TimeoutException after 0:01:00.000: Timed out waiting for gate-echo-marker-reply in output." — the harness's waitForText budget was 60s (30s × FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2). The screen showed "Working… 59s · submit".

So the CLI was working for 59s. The mock should answer instantly. Unless the request never reached the mock, OR the request reached the mock but the response was never processed, OR the CLI was stuck somewhere else entirely (e.g., the shift-HID poll! — this test is about the SSH gate: with SSH env, the Shift+Enter HID polling is disabled. The failure is in the FIRST phase: submit + reply).

Hmm wait, actually, let me reconsider: "Working… 59s" — the elapsed counter counts from submit. If the provider request hung on connect... to 127.0.0.1 — that can't hang on connect normally (localhost either connects or refuses). Unless the arm runner's loopback was saturated.

OR: the response arrived but the model's reply was classified EMPTY and the loop retried with backoff — 500ms+1s+2s+4s = 7.5s, then exhaustion error. That would end the turn in ~8s, not 59s.

OR: the completion arrived, and the turn continued into a TOOL call loop? The echo reply is "gate-echo-marker-reply" — no tool calls. 

OR the AOT binary failed to boot and the harness's waitForBoot passed on some early output, then the submit went nowhere. But the screen shows the full TUI booted (session path, model, endpoint). And the submitted message shows in the transcript row 15 " gate-echo-marker". The status "Working… 59s" means the run began.

So: request sent → no response processed for 59s. On an overloaded arm runner with 4 concurrent tests each spawning AOT CLI processes... the mock server is IN the test process — if the test process's event loop was busy (the harness polls the PTY screen with regex over ANSI output every X ms), the HttpServer might be starved? The test process runs pollUntil which awaits streams — the event loop stays live. The mock should still answer.

Unless the RESPONSE was answered but the SSE parsing on the CLI side didn't complete because the connection stayed open... the mock closes the response after [DONE]. Fine.

OK — I can't fully diagnose a timing flake from one artifact. Evidence so far:
1. Test passes locally (JIT).
2. Broad CI redness today across many branches, including main and release tags, on DIFFERENT legs (flutter app tests shard 0/2 on main, PTY here). 
3. The repo's PTY suite has a documented flake problem with a formal quarantine process.

Let me now check the shard's dart-test json artifact for the failing run — the per-test durations might show resource starvation (all tests slow). Also check whether OTHER ssh_shift_gate tests passed in the same shard ("FA_TUI_SHIFT_HID=0 without SSH env" PASSED in the same CI run — same mock, same spawn path, only the SSH env differs!). That's important: the second test in the SAME file with the SAME mock passed right after. So mock + spawn + submit + reply worked fine at 19:31:58. The difference: SSH_CONNECTION/SSH_TTY env vars → the shift-HID gate.

So the first test failed waiting for the REPLY — but the second test's reply came through fine seconds later. The reply path (mock→CLI→render) works. So in the failed test, either the submit didn't trigger a request, or the request/response raced.

Hmm — the SSH gate disables the HID poll. The submit path: sendText('gate-echo-marker') then sendEnter(). With SSH env, Enter submits (that's the test's assertion). If the Enter was eaten (PTY timing), the composer would still show the text and nothing would run — but the screen shows "Working… 59s", so the run DID start. The run started but never produced the reply.

Actually wait, let me look at the raw tail once more: "Working… 0s · submit" then the composer grid painting. The status row shows "Working… 0s" — at that frame the run had just started. Then nothing for 59s.

Hmm, what about this: the reply DID arrive and the run finished, but the transcript rendering of the reply happened... the screen at timeout shows "Working… 59s" — the status row says still Working at 59s. So the run genuinely hadn't finished at 59s.

A 59s hang in Working with a local mock. Connect timeout is 180s — if the request was never sent (queued behind something) or the socket connect blocked...

What in this PR could delay the FIRST request? Let me look at the full agent_loop diff for the streaming path. If e.g. the retry machinery wraps the stream call in a way that could stall... Let me read agent_loop_empty_completion.dart fully, plus the loop changes in agent_loop.dart.

The second test in the same file (same mock, same spawn, no SSH env) passed right after — so the mock and spawn path work. Let me study the loop diff for anything that could stall the first request, and check the per-test durations in the CI artifact.

blocks.text:
The repo has an established flake-quarantine mechanism: a PTY test that flakes in the gate gets quarantined (removed from deterministic legs) pending a fix, with a tracker issue and ≥2 distinct failing SHAs as proof.

The `ssh_shift_gate_test.dart` is not quarantined — but it may have just started flaking. Before quarantining (which is a workflow/manifest change and might beyond my remit), let me gather evidence:

1. Check if this test failed in OTHER recent CI runs (other branches) — the runs list shows many red runs today; let me check a few more pty legs from other branches to see if ssh_shift_gate failed there too. 

Actually, the runs I listed with status=failure only show one failing leg each. For runs on OTHER branches where pty-integration-linux passed, ssh_shift_gate passed. The question is whether ssh_shift_gate flaked elsewhere recently.

Let me look at the flake-watch tooling and recent nightly data. Actually — simpler: let me check the last ~20 pty-integration-linux job results on all branches and grep for ssh_shift_gate failures. That's a lot of API calls. Alternative: the flake_watch.py script probably reads test-results artifacts.

Alternatively, run the failing test repeatedly locally to see if it's reproducibly flaky under load. And also run the OTHER PTY tests in shard 2 that exercise similar paths.

Actually, wait. Let me think about the failure more carefully. A key detail in the log: the failing run was at 19:30-19:31. The whole shard ran from 19:30:04 to 19:32:00 — under 2 minutes for 112 tests?? Look: the first step timestamps: 19:30:04 runner provision, dart test started ~19:30:30?, failed test at 19:31:57, and the summary "111 tests passed, 1 failed" at 19:32:00. That's a very fast shard — plausible with concurrency=4 and the AOT binary (~1s per spawn).

Hmm wait, actually that seems too fast for 112 integration tests including perf_open_gate (3.7s) etc. But it's arm64 with concurrency 4. Plausible.

Now, the specific failure: "TimeoutException after 0:01:00.000: Timed out waiting for gate-echo-marker-reply in output." — the harness's waitForText budget was 60s (30s × FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2). The screen showed "Working… 59s · submit".

So the CLI was working for 59s. The mock should answer instantly. Unless the request never reached the mock, OR the request reached the mock but the response was never processed, OR the CLI was stuck somewhere else entirely (e.g., the shift-HID poll! — this test is about the SSH gate: with SSH env, the Shift+Enter HID polling is disabled. The failure is in the FIRST phase: submit + reply).

Hmm wait, actually, let me reconsider: "Working… 59s" — the elapsed counter counts from submit. If the provider request hung on connect... to 127.0.0.1 — that can't hang on connect normally (localhost either connects or refuses). Unless the arm runner's loopback was saturated.

OR: the response arrived but the model's reply was classified EMPTY and the loop retried with backoff — 500ms+1s+2s+4s = 7.5s, then exhaustion error. That would end the turn in ~8s, not 59s.

OR: the completion arrived, and the turn continued into a TOOL call loop? The echo reply is "gate-echo-marker-reply" — no tool calls. 

OR the AOT binary failed to boot and the harness's waitForBoot passed on some early output, then the submit went nowhere. But the screen shows the full TUI booted (session path, model, endpoint). And the submitted message shows in the transcript row 15 " gate-echo-marker". The status "Working… 59s" means the run began.

So: request sent → no response processed for 59s. On an overloaded arm runner with 4 concurrent tests each spawning AOT CLI processes... the mock server is IN the test process — if the test process's event loop was busy (the harness polls the PTY screen with regex over ANSI output every X ms), the HttpServer might be starved? The test process runs pollUntil which awaits streams — the event loop stays live. The mock should still answer.

Unless the RESPONSE was answered but the SSE parsing on the CLI side didn't complete because the connection stayed open... the mock closes the response after [DONE]. Fine.

OK — I can't fully diagnose a timing flake from one artifact. Evidence so far:
1. Test passes locally (JIT).
2. Broad CI redness today across many branches, including main and release tags, on DIFFERENT legs (flutter app tests shard 0/2 on main, PTY here). 
3. The repo's PTY suite has a documented flake problem with a formal quarantine process.

Let me now check the shard's dart-test json artifact for the failing run — the per-test durations might show resource starvation (all tests slow). Also check whether OTHER ssh_shift_gate tests passed in the same shard ("FA_TUI_SHIFT_HID=0 without SSH env" PASSED in the same CI run — same mock, same spawn path, only the SSH env differs!). That's important: the second test in the SAME file with the SAME mock passed right after. So mock + spawn + submit + reply worked fine at 19:31:58. The difference: SSH_CONNECTION/SSH_TTY env vars → the shift-HID gate.

So the first test failed waiting for the REPLY — but the second test's reply came through fine seconds later. The reply path (mock→CLI→render) works. So in the failed test, either the submit didn't trigger a request, or the request/response raced.

Hmm — the SSH gate disables the HID poll. The submit path: sendText('gate-echo-marker') then sendEnter(). With SSH env, Enter submits (that's the test's assertion). If the Enter was eaten (PTY timing), the composer would still show the text and nothing would run — but the screen shows "Working… 59s", so the run DID start. The run started but never produced the reply.

Actually wait, let me look at the raw tail once more: "Working… 0s · submit" then the composer grid painting. The status row shows "Working… 0s" — at that frame the run had just started. Then nothing for 59s.

Hmm, what about this: the reply DID arrive and the run finished, but the transcript rendering of the reply happened... the screen at timeout shows "Working… 59s" — the status row says still Working at 59s. So the run genuinely hadn't finished at 59s.

A 59s hang in Working with a local mock. Connect timeout is 180s — if the request was never sent (queued behind something) or the socket connect blocked...

What in this PR could delay the FIRST request? Let me look at the full agent_loop diff for the streaming path. If e.g. the retry machinery wraps the stream call in a way that could stall... Let me read agent_loop_empty_completion.dart fully, plus the loop changes in agent_loop.dart.

The second test in the same file (same mock, same spawn, no SSH env) passed right after — so the mock and spawn path work. Let me study the loop diff for anything that could stall the first request, and check the per-test durations in the CI artifact.

That's a very fast shard — plausible with concurrency=4 and the AOT binary (~1s per spawn).

Hmm wait, actually that seems too fast for 112 integration tests including perf_open_gate (3.7s) etc. But it's arm64 with concurrency 4. Plausible.

Now, the specific failure: "TimeoutException after 0:01:00.000: Timed out waiting for gate-echo-marker-reply in output." — the harness's waitForText budget was 60s (30s × FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2). The screen showed "Working… 59s · submit".

So the CLI was working for 59s. The mock should answer instantly. Unless the request never reached the mock, OR the request reached the mock but the response was never processed, OR the CLI was stuck somewhere else entirely (e.g., the shift-HID poll! — this test is about the SSH gate: with SSH env, the Shift+Enter HID polling is disabled. The failure is in the FIRST phase: submit + reply).

Hmm wait, actually, let me reconsider: "Working… 59s" — the elapsed counter counts from submit. If the provider request hung on connect... to 127.0.0.1 — that can't hang on connect normally (localhost either connects or refuses). Unless the arm runner's loopback was saturated.

OR: the response arrived but the model's reply was classified EMPTY and the loop retried with backoff — 500ms+1s+2s+4s = 7.5s, then exhaustion error. That would end the turn in ~8s, not 59s.

OR: the completion arrived, and the turn continued into a TOOL call loop? The echo reply is "gate-echo-marker-reply" — no tool calls. 

OR the AOT binary failed to boot and the harness's waitForBoot passed on some early output, then the submit went nowhere. But the screen shows the full TUI booted (session path, model, endpoint). And the submitted message shows in the transcript row 15 " gate-echo-marker". The status "Working… 59s" means the run began.

So: request sent → no response processed for 59s. On an overloaded arm runner with 4 concurrent tests each spawning AOT CLI processes... the mock server is IN the test process — if the test process's event loop was busy (the harness polls the PTY screen with regex over ANSI output every X ms), the HttpServer might be starved? The test process runs pollUntil which awaits streams — the event loop stays live. The mock should still answer.

Unless the RESPONSE was answered but the SSE parsing on the CLI side didn't complete because the connection stayed open... the mock closes the response after [DONE]. Fine.

OK — I can't fully diagnose a timing flake from one artifact. Evidence so far:

So the first test failed waiting for the REPLY — but the second test's reply came through fine seconds later. The reply path (mock→CLI→render) works. So in the failed test, either the submit didn't trigger a request, or the request/response raced.

The repo has an established flake-quarantine mechanism: a PTY test that flakes in the gate gets quarantined (removed from deterministic legs) pending a fix, with a tracker issue and ≥2 distinct failing SHAs as proof.

The `ssh_shift_gate_test.dart` is not quarantined — but it may have just started flaking. Before quarantining (which is a workflow/manifest change and might beyond my remit), let me gather evidence:

1. Check if this test failed in OTHER recent CI runs (other branches) — the runs list shows many red runs today; let me check a few more pty legs from other branches to see if ssh_shift_gate failed there too. 

Actually, the runs I listed with status=failure only show one failing leg each. For runs on OTHER branches where pty-integration-linux passed, ssh_shift_gate passed. The question is whether ssh_shift_gate flaked elsewhere recently.

Let me look at the flake-watch tooling and recent nightly data. Actually — simpler: let me check the last ~20 pty-integration-linux job results on all branches and grep for ssh_shift_gate failures. That's a lot of API calls. Alternative: the flake_watch.py script probably reads test-results artifacts.

Alternatively, run the failing test repeatedly locally to see if it's reproducibly flaky under load. And also run the OTHER PTY tests in shard 2 that exercise similar paths.

Actually, wait. Let me think about the failure more carefully. A key detail in the log: the failing run was at 19:30-19:31. The whole shard ran from 19:30:04 to 19:32:00 — under 2 minutes for 112 tests?? Look: the first step timestamps: 19:30:04 runner provision, dart test started ~19:30:30?, failed test at 19:31:57, and the summary "111 tests passed, 1 failed" at 19:32:00. That's a very fast shard — plausible with concurrency=4 and the AOT binary (~1s per spawn).

Hmm wait, actually that seems too fast for 112 integration tests including perf_open_gate (3.7s) etc. But it's arm64 with concurrency 4. Plausible.

Now, the specific failure: "TimeoutException after 0:01:00.000: Timed out waiting for gate-echo-marker-reply in output." — the harness's waitForText budget was 60s (30s × FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE=2). The screen showed "Working… 59s · submit".

So the CLI was working for 59s. The mock should answer instantly. Unless the request never reached the mock, OR the request reached the mock but the response was never processed, OR the CLI was stuck somewhere else entirely (e.g., the shift-HID poll! — this test is about the SSH gate: with SSH env, the Shift+Enter HID polling is disabled. The failure is in the FIRST phase: submit + reply).

Hmm wait, actually, let me reconsider: "Working… 59s" — the elapsed counter counts from submit. If the provider request hung on connect... to 127.0.0.1 — that can't hang on connect normally (localhost either connects or refuses). Unless the arm runner's loopback was saturated.

OR: the response arrived but the model's reply was classified EMPTY and the loop retried with backoff — 500ms+1s+2s+4s = 7.5s, then exhaustion error. That would end the turn in ~8s, not 59s.

OR: the completion arrived, and the turn continued into a TOOL call loop? The echo reply is "gate-echo-marker-reply" — no tool calls. 

OR the AOT binary failed to boot and the harness's waitForBoot passed on some early output, then the submit went nowhere. But the screen shows the full TUI booted (session path, model, endpoint). And the submitted message shows in the transcript row 15 " gate-echo-marker". The status "Working… 59s" means the run began.

So: request sent → no response processed for 59s. On an overloaded arm runner with 4 concurrent tests each spawning AOT CLI processes... the mock server is IN the test process — if the test process's event loop was busy (the harness polls the PTY screen with regex over ANSI output every X ms), the HttpServer might be starved? The test process runs pollUntil which awaits streams — the event loop stays live. The mock should still answer.

Unless the RESPONSE was answered but the SSE parsing on the CLI side didn't complete because the connection stayed open... the mock closes the response after [DONE]. Fine.

OK — I can't fully diagnose a timing flake from one artifact. Evidence so far:
1. Test passes locally (JIT).
2. Broad CI redness today across many branches, including main and release tags, on DIFFERENT legs (flutter app tests shard 0/2 on main, PTY here). 
3. The repo's PTY suite has a documented flake problem with a formal quarantine process.

Let me now check the shard's dart-test json artifact for the failing run — the per-test durations might show resource starvation (all tests slow). Also check whether OTHER ssh_shift_gate tests passed in the same shard ("FA_TUI_SHIFT_HID=0 without SSH env" PASSED in the same CI run — same mock, same spawn path, only the SSH env differs!). That's important: the second test in the SAME file with the SAME mock passed right after. So mock + spawn + submit + reply worked fine at 19:31:58. The difference: SSH_CONNECTION/SSH_TTY env vars → the shift-HID gate.

So the first test failed waiting for the REPLY — but the second test's reply came through fine seconds later. The reply path (mock→CLI→render) works. So in the failed test, either the submit didn't trigger a request, or the request/response raced.

Hmm — the SSH gate disables the HID poll. The submit path: sendText('gate-echo-marker') then sendEnter(). With SSH env, Enter submits (that's the test's assertion). If the Enter was eaten (PTY timing), the composer would still show the text and nothing would run — but the screen shows "Working… 59s", so the run DID start. The run started but never produced the reply.

Actually wait, let me look at the raw tail once more: "Working… 0s · submit" then the composer grid painting. The status row shows "Working… 0s" — at that frame the run had just started. Then nothing for 59s.

Hmm, what about this: the reply DID arrive and the run finished, but the transcript rendering of the reply happened... the screen at timeout shows "Working… 59s" — the status row says still Working at 59s. So the run genuinely hadn't finished at 59s.

A 59s hang in Working with a local mock. Connect timeout is 180s — if the request was never sent (queued behind something) or the socket connect blocked...

What in this PR could delay the FIRST request? Let me look at the full agent_loop diff for the streaming path. If e.g. the retry machinery wraps the stream call in a way that could stall... Let me read agent_loop_empty_completion.dart fully, plus the loop changes in agent_loop.dart.

The second test in the same file (same mock, same spawn, no SSH env) passed right after — so the mock and spawn path work. Let me study the loop diff for anything that could stall the first request, and check the per-test durations in the CI artifact.
